earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct unclassified Brazilian language known only from a short wordlist; no phonological description exists.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt & R. F. Mansur Guérios. 1948. Cartas etnolingüísticas. Revista do Museu Paulista, N.S. 2: 207-241. [Nimuendajú's letters of 1944 on Botocudo (Krenak), Kamakã and Kaingang, with his transcription key p. 224]
sources.note: Not a statement about Baenan. It documents that in Nimuendajú's own lists of this period the acute accent marks the stressed syllable, the only available clue for reading the four final-accented forms (bakurí, kelemés, kadašužé, pitirát) in the Baenan list; but Loukotka 1963 re-transcribed the notebook without comment, so no stress statement for baen1237 can be derived or quoted.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1/5.3, languoid baen1237 'Baenan' (Unclassifiable; extinct).
sources.note: No descriptive references at all (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology); only Wikipedia/Wikidata links.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Baenã language' (accessed 2026-09-17); cites Loukotka 1963, Meader 1978, Nelson 2018.
sources.note: Nothing; reproduces the 9-word list (secondary) and reports that by 1961 the last Baenã person, Rosalinda, could not provide any words of the language (citing Meader 1978).

sources.citation: Argolo, Wagner. 2024. Sul da Bahia: do multilinguismo ao unilinguismo (1760-1940). Revista do GEL 21(1): 197-223. doi:10.21165/gel.v21i1.3647 [section 'A viagem de Curt Nimuendaju ao sul da Bahia em 1938', item [iv] baenãs, p. 217]
sources.note: no phonology content; socio-historical article summarizing the unpublished Nimuendajú 1938 report.

sources.citation: Campbell, Lyle. 2024. Unclassified and Spurious Languages. Chapter 5 of: The Indigenous Languages of the Americas: History and Classification, pp. 280-338. New York: Oxford University Press. DOI 10.1093/oso/9780197673461.003.0005.
sources.note: ten words known, too few to classify; no statement: nothing on stress, accent or tone anywhere in the chapter (the words stress/accent/tone/pitch/syllable do not occur); entry concerns attestation and classification only

sources.citation: Ferreira, Talita Almeida. 2017. Contato, territorialização e conflito no Posto Indígena Caramuru-Paraguassú: o SPI e os Baenã, Gueren, Kamakan, Maxakali, Pataxó, e índios de antigos aldeamentos no sul da Bahia, 1910-1936. Dissertação (Mestrado em História), Universidade Federal Rural do Rio de Janeiro. 229 pp.
sources.note: no phonology content; history thesis built on SPI reports; only an impressionistic journalist's remark (Carneiro 1936) that Baenã and Hãhãhãe had 'sing-song speech with clenched teeth'. Supplies the alternative ethnonym Nóc-noács and the Jacobina 1934 pointer.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 2017 [1944]. Mapa etno-histórico do Brasil e regiões adjacentes. 2a edição (coord. Jorge Domingues Lopes & Marcus Vinícius Carvalho Garcia). Brasília: IPHAN / IBGE. [Índice de tribos p. 57: 'Baenã(4) : G 6 : 4. 761.'; 1a ed. IBGE 1981]
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: nothing; pointer only. Confirms that Nimuendajú himself left the Baenã linguistically unlabelled and did not count them among the languages he had samples of.

sources.citation: Carvalho, Maria Rosário de. 2016. Curt Nimuendaju no sul da Bahia: registro etnográfico e repercussões de sua visita aos Pataxó Hãhãhãi. R@U – Revista de Antropologia da UFSCar 8(2): 67-85. [section 'Os Baenã', pp. 79-80, paraphrasing and quoting Nimuendajú's unpublished 10-page 1938 report/letter, Ilhéus 8 Dec 1938]
sources.note: no phonology content; the closest reading of Nimuendajú's own 1938 report confirms he obtained no Baenã speech at all (only an arrow). Fn. 8: Loukotka 1954: 1034 cites a Nimuendajú letter of 10 May 1940 saying no informant knew the old language.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri; Valdir Vegini & Maria Cristina Victorino de França. 2015. Koropó, puri, kamakã e outras línguas do Leste Brasileiro. LIAMES: Línguas Indígenas Americanas 15(2): 223-277. doi:10.20396/liames.v15i2.8642302
sources.note: Name appears only in the closing classification list of East-Brazilian languages as incertae sedis; no data, no phonology.

sources.citation: Souza, Jurema Machado de Andrade & Maria Rosário G. de Carvalho. 2005/2018. 'Pataxó Hã-Hã-Hãe'. Povos Indígenas no Brasil, Instituto Socioambiental (section 'Baenã'; last modified 2021-01-20).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content; encyclopedia entry summarizing Nimuendajú 1938 and Jacobina 1932/1934; its source list gave the pointers to Nimuendajú 1958 (RA 6(1): 53-61, = Maxakalí report, checked: nothing on Baenã), the 8-Dec-1938 letter and Jacobina 1934.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 2000. Cartas do Sertão: de Curt Nimuendajú para Carlos Estevão de Oliveira. Apresentação e notas de Thekla Hartmann. Lisboa: Museu Nacional de Etnologia / Assírio & Alvim. 397 pp. [A cited this volume under work 3 as the print home of the 8-Dec-1938 letter; it is open and does not contain it]
sources.note: nothing; no Baenã content at all. Corrects A: the 1938 letter with the Baenã paragraph is not in this (open) volume.

sources.citation: Grupioni, Luís Donisete Benzi. 1998. Coleções e expedições vigiadas: os etnólogos no Conselho de Fiscalização das Expedições Artísticas e Científicas no Brasil. São Paulo: Hucitec/Anpocs. 341 pp. [ch. 'Viagem à Bahia, a Minas Gerais e ao Espírito Santo', pp. 189-197, with excerpts of Nimuendajú's letter of Ilhéus 8 Dec 1938]
sources.note: nothing on phonology; only Nimuendajú's classificatory remark that none of these Bahia groups is Gê. Fn 36 (p. 195): Carlos Estevão's personal papers, 'entre os quais várias cartas e manuscritos de Nimuendajú', were donated to the Museu do Estado de Pernambuco, a second possible repository of the 1938 letter. 74 MB PDF not kept (three passing mentions); extract.

sources.citation: Meader, Robert E. 1978. Indios do Nordeste: levantamento sobre os remanescentes tribais do nordeste brasileiro. (Série Lingüística 8.) Brasília: SIL.
sources.note: SIL survey of remnant groups of the Northeast; per Wikipedia it records that the last Baenã person (Rosalinda, 1961) could give no words, so it likely contains no Baenã data, but it should be checked for any residual forms or remarks.

sources.citation: Edelweiss, Frederico. 1971. Curt Nimuendaju na Bahia. Universitas (Salvador, UFBA) 8/9: 277-280. [prints Nimuendajú's letter-report to Edelweiss, Belém do Pará, 15 Aug 1939; item 2 on the Baenã]
sources.note: no phonology content; Nimuendajú's own first-hand statement that the language was unclassified and unrecorded.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. p. 74, entry '21. Baenan, isolated language'.
sources.note: Nothing; the entry gives only location ('originally spoken between the Cachoeira and Pardo Rivers, state of Bahia, now only by a few individuals on the Posto Paraguaçú') and cites Loukotka 1963 p. 54 and 'Nimuendajú ms.n.'; no words, no phonology.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1963. Documents et vocabulaires inédits de langues et de dialectes sud-américains. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 52: 7-60. §62 'Langue dont le nom indigène est inconnu', p. 54.
sources.note: Nothing. Prints the 9 words Nimuendajú recorded in 1938 (from his notebook 'Kamakan-Material II', SPI archive, Rio), which R. D. Carneiro attributed to the Baenan tribe: eželẽ 'cerf', bakurí 'chevreuil', kelemés 'feu', patarak 'jaguar', kadašužé 'nègre', bonikro 'porc', pititiŋga 'rat', pitirát 'singe', šẽšẽ 'taureau'. Four words carry an acute accent on the final syllable, five carry no mark; no note on what the accents mean and no remark on stress anywhere in the article (pp. 7-8 introduction checked). page scan downloaded from the open Persée viewer; the PDF download is behind an altcha ch…

sources.citation: Ribeiro, Darcy. 1957. Culturas e línguas indígenas do Brasil. Educação e Ciências Sociais 2(6): 1-102. Rio de Janeiro: Centro Brasileiro de Pesquisas Educacionais. [p. 71 entry BAENAN; p. 32 on undocumented extinct 'línguas alófilas']
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: nothing; classifies Baenân as a language of its own stock ('Baenãn') that vanished without documentation adequate even for classification.

sources.citation: Nelson, Jessica Fae. 2018. Pataxó Hãhãhãe: Race, Indigeneity and Language Revitalization in the Brazilian Northeast. PhD dissertation, University of Arizona.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Modern ethnographic/sociolinguistic account of the Pataxó Hãhãhãe, of whom the Baenã are now a subgroup; may summarize the historical record of Baenã but cannot contain new phonological data.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1938. 'Kamakan-Material II', manuscript notebook, formerly SPI central archive, Rio de Janeiro (now presumably Museu do Índio / Nimuendajú papers).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The sole primary record of the 9 words; the original could show whether the acute accents are Nimuendajú's stress marks and whether any note on accent accompanies them. Would not yield a general stress rule.

The Indigenous Languages of the Americas: History and Classification. Oxford University Press ['Baenan Brazil. Known from only ten words']
